text_blocks.snippet: Listerine, as a mouthwash, is designed to help prevent and reduce oral bacteria, which can contribute to infections, but it is not a treatment for existing infections, especially those requiring professional dental or medical care. While it can kill bacteria in the mouth, it's not a substitute for proper treatment of conditions like tooth or gum infections.
snippet_highlighted_words: it is not a treatment for existing infections

list.title: Reduces bacteria:
list.snippet: Listerine contains ingredients like thymol, eucalyptol, menthol, and methyl salicylate, which are essential oils that can kill bacteria, including those that cause plaque and gingivitis.

list.title: Helps prevent infections:
list.snippet: By reducing the bacterial load in the mouth, Listerine can help prevent the development of infections, especially in individuals with a higher risk.

list.title: May help with minor cuts:
list.snippet: Some people use Listerine to help clean minor cuts or wounds, but it is important to consult with a healthcare professional for more serious wounds or infections.

list.title: Not a treatment for infections:
list.snippet: Listerine cannot penetrate deep enough into tissues to treat existing infections like tooth or gum abscesses.

list.title: May not be effective for all infections:
list.snippet: While it can kill some bacteria, it may not be effective against all types of infections, especially those requiring specific antibiotics or other treatments.

list.title: Potential for side effects:
list.snippet: Excessive or improper use of Listerine can cause side effects like mouth irritation, dryness, or altered taste.

list.title: Tooth or gum infections:
list.snippet: If you have signs of infection like tooth pain, swollen gums, or pus, you should see a dentist or doctor for proper diagnosis and treatment.

list.title: Open sores or wounds:
list.snippet: If you have open sores or wounds, consult with a healthcare professional before using any mouthwash, including Listerine.

list.title: Fungal infections:
list.snippet: If you have a persistent fungal infection on your feet or toenails, see a doctor, especially if you have underlying medical conditions like diabetes.

related_questions.question: Can mouthwash be used as a disinfectant?

text_blocks.snippet: Yes, certain types of mouthwash, particularly those containing antiseptic ingredients like alcohol, can be used as a disinfectant for some household surfaces. Mouthwash was initially developed as a surgical disinfectant before being adapted for oral hygiene. Its antiseptic and antibacterial properties make it useful for cleaning and disinfecting various items and surfaces.
snippet_highlighted_words: Yes, certain types of mouthwash, particularly those containing antiseptic ingredients like alcohol, can be used as a disinfectant for some household surfaces

text_blocks.snippet: Here's how mouthwash can be used as a disinfectant:

list.title: Toothbrush disinfection:
list.snippet: Soaking a toothbrush in antiseptic mouthwash can help kill bacteria.

list.title: Cleaning toilet bowls:
list.snippet: Half a cup of mouthwash can be used to clean and disinfect toilet bowls, according to Albion Dental Center.

list.title: Cleaning grout and removing stains:
list.snippet: An old toothbrush dipped in mouthwash can be used to clean grout, remove hard water stains, and inhibit mold growth.

list.title: Shining mirrors and disinfecting surfaces:
list.snippet: A lint-free cloth dampened with mouthwash can be used to clean and disinfect mirrors, doorknobs, and other surfaces.

list.title: Cleaning screens:
list.snippet: Alcohol-based mouthwash can be used to clean dirt and fingerprints from screens.

list.title: Alcohol content:
list.snippet: Many mouthwashes contain alcohol, which is an effective disinfectant. However, some people may find alcohol-based mouthwashes irritating says Hollymead Dental Arts. If you have sensitive skin or prefer alcohol-free options, you may want to choose an alternative disinfectant.

list.title: Not a substitute for hand sanitizer:
list.snippet: While mouthwash can be used for surface disinfection, it's not a substitute for hand sanitizer, especially when it comes to preventing the spread of viruses. Public health authorities recommend frequent handwashing with soap and water as the primary method for hand hygiene.

list.title: Consider the ingredients:
list.snippet: Some mouthwashes contain specific ingredients like chlorhexidine or hydrogen peroxide, which have antiseptic and disinfectant properties.

text_blocks.snippet: In summary, while mouthwash can be a useful tool for disinfecting certain household items, it's important to consider its alcohol content and other ingredients, and to prioritize handwashing with soap and water for overall hygiene.
